searches.note: Twenty three searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h2, none of them the author's; five left unspent. Five were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain and read through their summaries: maisons-champagne.com with champagne-deutz.com (the chronology), champagne-deutz.com (the philosophy page, the vats), champagne-drappier.com twice (the Charles de Gaulle sheet and the history page; the Grande Sendrée sheets) and one with dreyfusashby.com. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries.

tested.founded: 1584, an alderman of Aÿ making still wines, mostly red: the house, Wilson Daniels, Hachette. The founder is Pierre in most accounts and Jean in one, so he stays described.
tested.story: The end of 1993 for the Renaud-Cointreau group: the house and Wilson Daniels; Hachette and LSA give 1994, said in the report. The clear rosé bottle: the house's claim, credited by two trade accounts to Suzanne Gosset in 1947; her presidency of 1955 to 1965 is consistent across them. The move to Épernay in 2009 stands on the library and the house.
tested.cuvee: First vintage 1988 released 1995: the Drinks Business, World of Fine Wine. The 2012 the ninth since 1988, 70 per cent Chardonnay: the same. 2008: 54 and 46, 4.8 grams a litre, steel, no malolactic, no oak (Wilson Daniels, Falstaff, Millesima; two merchants give 8 and 3 grams, outliers). The Blanc de Blancs 2012: Falstaff. The 1988's 9 grams rested on one report: cut.
tested.table: cuvee45 said the house counts only nine vintages, true only until the next; house45's never was an absolute: both fixed.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read; the third explanation taught a claim with no source: fixed.

open: The founder is Pierre Gosset in the house's and the importer's accounts and Jean Gosset in one merchant's, which is why he stays described, not named.
The clear rosé bottle is dated 1947 by two trade accounts, before the woman's presidency of 1955 to 1965; the record keeps it undated as the house's claim.
Whether the 2012 label reads Brut or Extra Brut: the importer and one critic say Brut, a merchant Extra Brut.
